transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Kaur (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Elmstone CTO), Asha Patel (ML Platform), Diego Ramos (SRE), Leah Wong (Product)

Summary (auto): Jordan runs through parity plan to move Elmstone’s endpoints from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API. Heavy focus on preserving prompt/response schema, latency SLOs, and encryption/KMS integration. Questions about dedicated pools, burst capacity, and token accounting for billing.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Marcus: yeah good, loud and clear. sorry caught a flight but i'm on my laptop.
[00:10] Jordan: awesome, we'll run a 60 minute walkthrough. quick intros — i'm Jordan, AE on Redwood, priya and samir from solutions, they'll handle the console and tech deep dive.
[00:20] Asha: hi all, i'm Asha, i own the platform team at Elmstone. we're evaluating lift and shift for a number of endpoints.
[00:25] Leah: Leah, product — i'll chime on success criteria and latency.
[00:30] Priya: quick agenda — parity mapping, demo the API switchover + console, then optimize suggestions (batching/quant), then Q&A and next steps.

[02:15] Jordan: to start, what's your current footprint — you mentioned OpenAI + Anthropic + Together in the docs. can you give rough split and what you care about?
[02:30] Marcus: sure, roughly 60% OpenAI for customer-facing chat, 25% Anthropic for compliance-sensitive summarization, and 15% Together for internal embeddings and cheaper batch jobs. latency is critical for chat (under 200ms token p99 ideally) but cost is also a big driver. we also have CCPA and EU data residency concerns for some products.
[02:50] Diego: and our infra — most traffic goes to cloud endpoints today, but we have a VPC in AWS and an air-gapped staging environment for sensitive models.

[05:00] Priya: ok good context. our approach with Redwood is to give you the same API semantics (we map generative endpoints, chat, embeddings, rerank) — parity usually breaks into three buckets: API surface changes, response shape differences (tokenization), and perf/cost tuning (batching, kv cache).
[05:30] Marcus: how often do you see tokenization change break prompts?
[05:40] Priya: occasionally — models differ (many open models use different BPEs), so in our migration playbook we include a tokenization audit and small prompt adjustments. we provide a tokenizer diff report and suggested prompt rewrite.

[07:15] Samir: demo time — i'll drop into the console. note: i might say redwood private/dedicated slightly wrong, the auto transcription sometimes shows "red wood" ha.
[07:25] (screen share noise)
[07:40] Samir: console nav — Projects -> Models -> Routes. here's the existing route mapping we set up for a demo tenant. you can pin model versions, set rollout policies (canary, A/B), and route by policy — latency, cost or region.
[08:10] Leah: can you show how to force fallback to a cheaper quantized variant if the primary is saturated?
[08:20] Samir: yeah — under the route you add a fallback chain. e.g., openai-gptlike -> redwood-gptq -> redwood-7b-quant. the routing engine will failover automatically based on latency SLOs or if a region is down.

[10:00] Marcus: what about consistent KV cache behavior? we use long conversations and we rely on KV cache reuse.
[10:15] Priya: our runtime exposes KV cache controls; you can configure prefix caching and per-route cache TTLs. for parity we replicate your current cache hit heuristics, but there's sometimes a small tuning window for window sizes and the kernel selection (attention optimizations).

[12:45] Asha: security — we need KMS with HSM-backed keys, SSO via SAML, and audit logs for every token-level call.
[12:55] Jordan: yes — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, bring-your-own HSM). we also have SAML SSO + RBAC, and you can export audit logs to your SIEM. we'll share the SOC2 + ISO artifacts after the call.

[15:00] Priya: switching to cost parity — we built a quick spreadsheet from the traces you shared, the big levers are batching for embedding jobs, quantization for non-evaluative chat, and caching for repeated prefixes. for Together-style cheap batch jobs, the quantized 4-bit routes usually give 3-4x cost reduction vs float32.
[15:30] Marcus: ok — but latency for chat users is a blocker for quantization right?
[15:40] Priya: depends — with newer kernel paths and optimized compilation we can hit low latency with certain int8 paths, but there's a tradeoff. that’s why we recommend a canary: route small percent to quantized and run A/B on quality.

[18:00] Samir: pulling up an example migration diff — old prompt + openai response vs redwood response. note: transcription may show "K-V cash" sometimes.
[18:20] (short pause)
[18:30] Marcus: i'm seeing a slight paraphrase here, about ~2% quality delta on the summarization endpoint — is there an eval harness you use?
[18:40] Priya: yes — Redwood Optimize includes eval suites tied to prompts. we run regression checks and surface failures per-prompt. we'll set thresholds you care about and block rollout if QA falls below X.

[21:15] Leah: operationally — how much effort is the initial adapter work? we have ~12 endpoints across product and support.
[21:30] Jordan: most customers do a phased approach: pick 3-4 high-traffic endpoints for the pilot, run parity tests and a 1-week benchmark, then expand. adapters (if you have custom preprocessing) are usually small — ~1-2 engineer-weeks per major endpoint.

[24:00] Diego: connectivity — how does Private (VPC) work vs Dedicated? we want traffic to stay inside our VPC for sensitive models.
[24:15] Priya: Redwood Private deploys a customer-managed control plane with private peering into your VPC; inference can run on customer-hosted nodes or on our dedicated pools but with private networking. Dedicated is our reserved GPU pools in Redwood's infra with tenancy guarantees — less networking integration but easier ops. We can run a hybrid where sensitive models are on Private and general models hit Dedicated.

[27:45] Marcus: what about audits and data retention for EU customers? we need GDPR records of processing and regional model hosting.
[28:00] Jordan: we support region pinning for model hosting and data residency. audit logs can be retained per your retention SLA — we have add-on packages for extended retention. we'll include the legal/compliance addendum examples.

[31:10] Priya: time for a short live API parity example. i'll call the Redwood API with a sample prompt translated from your OpenAI usage. note: the endpoint path is /v1/generate; we accept chat messages as messages[] and support function/tool calling.
[31:30] (keyboard noises)
[32:00] Priya: response looks similar — tokenization diff is 1-2 tokens for this prompt. quality score we run locally shows parity 98% on the acceptance metric you defined (semantic similarity).
[33:00] Asha: great, can we get the tokenizer diff reports for our corpus?
[33:10] Priya: yes we'll run a corpus scan in the pilot and deliver a tokenization audit + suggested prompt edits.

[36:00] Samir: quick note on metrics — console exposes token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and crew-level tracing for debugging. you can also hook in custom webhooks for failures.
[36:20] Diego: what's the billing model for dedicated burst capacity?
[36:30] Jordan: dedicated is typically a monthly commit with burst credits. burst is charged at a discounted overage rate; we can show a modeled cost vs your current spend in the parity spreadsheet.

[39:45] Marcus: i'm worried about model fallback causing inconsistent user experiences — if one variant is cheaper but lower quality it'll degrade chat.
[39:55] Priya: that's why we recommend staged rollouts and auto-rollback policies. Rollouts have QA gates from Optimize; if quality dips above threshold we rollback and notify. Also you can set per-route policies to avoid fallbacks for user-facing chat and only allow for background tasks.

[42:10] Leah: what are typical runtimes for a bench of 1000 chat messages on your dedicated 8-GPU pool vs OpenAI?
[42:25] Priya: ballpark: p50 token latency comparable, p95 depends on window size. we'll run an apples-to-apples benchmark during the pilot (we need your trace with token timing).

[45:00] Jordan: ok let's talk pilot scope — Priya, proposed pilot: 3 endpoints (chat, summarization, embeddings), 1 week of parallel traffic, run model variants (float32 vs q4/8) and collect quality metrics. Elmstone provides anonymized traces and prompt set. Redwood provides benchmark infra and a report.
[45:25] Asha: sounds good, timeline?
[45:30] Jordan: if we kick off week of 11/15, we can deliver a report by 11/22. pre-reqs: traces by 11/10, initial security questionnaire signed.

[48:00] Marcus: on the security questionnaire — we need to confirm KMS flow when keys are customer-managed. does Redwood ever touch plaintext?
[48:15] Jordan: no — with customer KMS the keys never leave your control; we decrypt in an enclave if required or you can run inference in your VPC to keep data on-prem. we'll include a technical note.

[50:00] Diego: small nit — do you support per-token-level throttling and how does rate limiting affect streaming?
[50:10] Samir: yes you can set token or request-level quotas. streaming remains live; if throttled the connection will get a 429 with backoff hints.

[53:00] Priya: last bit — Optimize recommendations are auto-suggested in console after we ingest traces: batching window, quantization candidate models, cache TTLs. there's also an optimization preview where you can simulate cost impact without changing live traffic.

[55:30] Leah: ok let's recap and owners.
[55:40] Jordan: recap: Jordan -> send parity/cost spreadsheet and legal docs by 11/08; Priya -> benchmark harness and tokenizer audit plan by 11/12; Marcus -> provide anonymized traces by 11/10. Schedule pilot week of 11/15.
[56:00] Marcus: confirmed, we'll try for 11/10 on traces.
[56:10] Asha: also add a short 1-hour onboarding for our infra team during pilot.

[58:00] Jordan: noted. urls i'm dropping in chat: migration playbook: https://redwood.ai/docs/migration-playbook (demo link), security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 and the cost template: https://redwood.ai/templates/parity-cost.csv (we'll email a customized sheet).

[60:00] Marcus: thanks all this was useful.
[60:05] Priya: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[60:30] (call ends)
